answer.rationale: Activation is down 6% QoQ and onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ. Memory_91 shows activation messaging inside the product improved week-one engagement and nudged accounts to first meaningful action—this directly addresses the activation decline. Memory_86 shows simplified onboarding improved completion, but memory_31 (verified) will confirm whether signup-field simplification remains a durable lift or if that effect has plateaued. Activation messaging is lower-risk than promotional pricing (memory_73 showed SMB discounts hurt retention at -12% despite signup gains) and addresses the core metric decline rather than competing on price against a new entrant. A standard experiment on activation messaging preserves optionality: if it works, we solve activation headwind; if it doesn't, we retain the option to test onboarding or enterprise sales assist in future cycles. Referral incentives (memory_57) work for established customers but won't move the activation or onboarding needle for new accounts in the current downturn. The competitive pricing pressure argues against promotional_pricing given memory_73's retention hit and our need for sustainable revenue.
